Running N on a finite input sequence xs starts from the initial global state N.a4, updates all nodes simultaneously left to right for each element of xs via N.a5, and applies N.a6 to the resulting global state.

The specific system N' = N.d14 T has node set Fin T × N.A1 (pairs (j, m) with 0 ≤ j < T and m a node of N). Each node (j, m) has local state type N.A3 m and initial state N.a4 m. Its readout function returns N.a6 N.a4 if T = 0, and otherwise applies N.a6 to the final layer's state assignment m ↦ σ(T - 1, m).

The three properties asserted of N' = N.d14 T are:
1. In particular, neither self-loops nor longer directed dependency cycles exist.
2. Output agreement up to length T (S1.D5 T (N.d14 T) N): For every finite input sequence xs of elements of X with length at most T, running N' on xs produces the same element of Y as running N on xs. (Agreement is not required for sequences of length strictly greater than T.)
3. Node count ((N.d14 T).d13 = T * N.d13): The cardinality of the finite node set of N' equals T times the cardinality of the finite node set of N.

translation:
Target names the following proposition (without asserting or proving it): For all types X and Y, every system N of type S1 X Y, and every natural number T (with no further restrictions on X, Y, N, or T—for example, T may be 0 and X or Y may be empty), the specific constructed system N' = N.d14 T satisfies the conjunction of three properties.

Here, a system N of type S1 X Y consists of a finite type of nodes N.A1; a local state type N.A3 n and an initial state N.a4 n for each node n; a simultaneous transition rule N.a5 assigning to each node n, global state σ (a choice of state in N.A3 m for every node m), and input x in X a next state in N.A3 n; and a readout function N.a6 mapping global states to Y. Running N on a finite input sequence xs starts from the initial global state N.a4, updates all nodes simultaneously left to right for each element of xs via N.a5, and applies N.a6 to the resulting global state.

The specific system N' = N.d14 T has node set Fin T × N.A1 (pairs (j, m) with 0 ≤ j < T and m a node of N). Each node (j, m) has local state type N.A3 m and initial state N.a4 m. On global state σ and input x, node (0, n) updates to N.a5 n N.a4 x (ignoring σ and using N's initial state), whereas for j > 0 node (j, n) updates to N.a5 n applied to the previous layer's state assignment m ↦ σ(j - 1, m) and input x. Its readout function returns N.a6 N.a4 if T = 0, and otherwise applies N.a6 to the final layer's state assignment m ↦ σ(T - 1, m).

The three properties asserted of N' = N.d14 T are:
1. Acyclicity of functional dependencies ((N.d14 T).D9): For every node a of N', there is no nonempty finite chain a = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = a (with k ≥ 1) such that at each step c_{i+1}'s update function genuinely depends on c_i's state—meaning there exist two global states σ, σ' of N' agreeing on all nodes other than c_i and an input x in X such that the update of c_{i+1} gives different values on (σ, x) and (σ', x). In particular, neither self-loops nor longer directed dependency cycles exist.
2. Output agreement up to length T (S1.D5 T (N.d14 T) N): For every finite input sequence xs of elements of X with length at most T, running N' on xs produces the same element of Y as running N on xs. (Agreement is not required for sequences of length strictly greater than T.)
3. Node count ((N.d14 T).d13 = T * N.d13): The cardinality of the finite node set of N' equals T times the cardinality of the finite node set of N.

Note that Target asserts these three properties specifically for the explicitly defined system N.d14 T, rather than merely asserting the existence of some system with these properties.

divergences.description: Finite time horizon T: P2 as worded in P-D53 (and the general statement in P-D52a) asserts the existence of a feedforward system with 'the same input-output function' without a horizon restriction, whereas Target introduces a finite horizon T, makes the unrolled system N.d14 T depend on T, and asserts agreement only on input sequences of length at most T (S1.D5 T rather than unbounded equivalence S1.D6). Although this is strictly weaker than unbounded equivalence (and declared by the author), it aligns with the finite-duration unrolling-through-time justification in P-H10 (e.g., 100 copies for 1 second at 10 ms resolution) and the behavioural-experiment framing in P-D52a.

Idealized system model: S1 X Y models systems as finite-node, discrete-time, deterministic, synchronous state machines with a fixed initial state, whereas the source passages speak more generally of recurrent and feedforward networks or physical systems (which could be continuous-time, asynchronous, or stochastic, though P-H10 already idealizes to discrete timesteps).

Quantification over all systems: Target quantifies over all systems N : S1 X Y (including non-recurrent ones and edge cases such as T = 0 or empty X), whereas the source passages restrict attention to recurrent networks/systems. This is a harmless strengthening (and declared by the author).

Explicit witness instead of existential claim: P-D53 (P2) states existentially that 'there exist feedforward systems' with the same input-output function, whereas Target asserts the properties for the single explicitly defined system N.d14 T. This is a harmless strengthening that reflects P-H10's specific unrolling construction.

Functional vs. structural feedforwardness and operational details of d14: Feedforwardness (D9) is formalized as acyclicity of single-node functional sensitivity (D7/D8) rather than physical wiring, and to handle variable sequence lengths up to T with a fixed readout at layer T - 1, N.d14 T broadcasts each input simultaneously to all T layers (so shorter sequences of length L < T are carried through layers T - L to T - 1 rather than starting at layer 0, and T = 0 yields an empty network with a constant readout).

Node-count conjunct vs. copy structure: The third conjunct of Target explicitly asserts only the cardinality equality (N.d14 T).d13 = T * N.d13, leaving the fact that N.d14 T actually consists of T copies of N's units (with matching local state spaces and transition rules) inside the definition of d14 itself.

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the recurrent-to-feedforward direction of P2 via unrolling through time as described in the sources, establishing acyclicity, T-step input-output equivalence, and T-fold unit scaling for an explicit unrolled construction. The main caveats are the explicit finite horizon T (implicit in P-H10's unrolling justification but absent from P2's bare wording) and standard modeling idealizations to finite, discrete-time, deterministic, synchronous systems.
